parameters.content:
## $0 by design — same copy/paste pattern as Phase 1-2, 5, 6

No Anthropic API key here either. Pauses on a form showing you the Shorts
Factory's exact system prompt (Agent #9 in 03-AGENT-PROMPTS.md) — copy it
into your own Claude.ai / Claude Code chat, then paste the JSON back.

## Runs in parallel with Phase 6, not after it

Per 01-ARCHITECTURE.md, Shorts and Thumbnail both branch off the same
QC-passed video — this does NOT depend on Phase 6 having run first.

## Gate fixed: qc_passed_at, not stage (2026-09-02)

Originally gated on `videos.stage = 'qc_passed'`, same as Phase 6. Live
test exposed the real problem: Phase 6's own completion advances `stage`
to `thumbnail_ready`, so running Phase 6 before this phase broke the gate
— Get Video found 0 rows and the branch silently terminated (no error,
logged as a fast 'Succeeded' execution that actually did nothing past
Get Video). Fixed by gating on `videos.qc_passed_at is not null` instead —
a timestamp Phase 5 sets once and never overwrites — so this phase and
Phase 6 can truly run in either order or in parallel off the same video.
Trade-off: nothing stops this phase being run twice for the same video —
no duplicate-guard was added, since neither phase had one before either.

## "Transcript with timestamps" — approximate, derived from the script itself

There's no real ASR/transcription step in this pipeline. Instead this
parses the `[BEAT] (~Ns, M words)` headers already in the Phase 2 final
script and turns their durations into cumulative start/end seconds per
beat. It's an honest approximation sourced from real data (the Story
Architect's own beat timing), not invented — but it will drift from the
actual rendered video's real timing once Assembly's pacing differs from
the script's estimate. Don't treat these seconds as frame-accurate.

The parser was rewritten (2026-09-02): it originally used a regex
lookahead requiring a literal blank line (`\n\n`) before the next `[BEAT]`
header to know where one beat's text ended. Real scripts don't reliably
have that blank line, so it silently matched only the first beat and
dumped the entire rest of the script into that beat's `text` field —
discovered live when the pasted transcript showed exactly that. Now it
finds all header positions first, then slices the text between each pair
of headers directly, which doesn't depend on any particular whitespace
convention.

## Schema change made for this phase

`shorts` had no column for the narration text or source timestamp range
(only `title`/`hook`/`storage_url`). Added `narration`, `cta`,
`source_start_seconds`, `source_end_seconds` via migration rather than
overloading an existing text field (unlike Phase 6's thumbnails, which had
to pack concept text into `variant_label` for lack of a better column).

## Before running this

1. Requires a video with `qc_passed_at` set (Phase 5 must have passed for
   this topic first).
2. Reuses the **Supabase account** credential — wire it into every HTTP
   node that hits `/rest/v1/...`.
3. Activate, open the Form Trigger's Production URL, enter the exact Topic
   Title.
4. On completion: 3-8 rows inserted into `shorts` (`status: 'pending'`,
   `storage_url: null` — this phase writes scripts, not rendered video).
   `videos.stage` is left untouched; Shorts don't gate the main pipeline.
